case.question: Explain two ways to notice recurring mistakes during untimed cube practice. Then write exactly one sentence in its own paragraph inviting Jules to practise on Friday.
case.expected: Two distinct untimed approaches and an independently separated paragraph containing exactly one invitation sentence with Jules and Friday.

models.answer:
Two ways to notice recurring mistakes in untimed practice are to review your solves slowly and deliberately—pausing after each one to identify where you hesitated or lost time—and to keep a simple log of the errors that repeat, such as the same F2L case or the same pause before PLL, so patterns become visible over several sessions.

Jules, would you like to practise together on Friday?

To spot recurring mistakes during untimed practice, review your solves for repeated patterns such as pausing at the same F2L slot or leaning on the same slow OLL algorithm, and note where your times consistently stall, such as a habitual hesitation before PLL—and Jules, would you like to practise together on Friday?

case.question: Explain two ways to notice recurring mistakes during untimed cube practice. Then write exactly one sentence in its own paragraph inviting Jules to practise on Friday.
case.expected: Two distinct untimed approaches and an independently separated paragraph containing exactly one invitation sentence with Jules and Friday.

models.answer:
Two ways to notice recurring mistakes in untimed practice are to review your solves slowly and deliberately—pausing after each one to identify where time was lost or a step felt uncertain—and to keep a simple log of the errors you spot, so repeated patterns (such as the same F2L case or a hesitant PLL recognition) become visible across sessions.

Jules, would you like to practise together on Friday?

One way to notice recurring mistakes during untimed practice is to replay each solve slowly and mark exactly where you hesitated, regripped or paused to think, and another is to keep a short written log after each session that names the repeated pattern, such as the same awkward F2L case, a slow cross or a fumbled last-layer recognition.

Jules, would you like to practise together this Friday?
